statement: Because LIFE-CODE independently recovered an exact primitive at one side of the ribosomal peptide-bond-forming machinery, the existing frozen three-domain raw-sequence corpus should contain another reusable primitive or nested primitive associated with the universally conserved A2451-centered peptidyl-transferase active-site neighborhood, even though that neighborhood was not used to create the original blind discovery.
test: Before any biological annotation, recover the complete list of frozen three-domain shared exact primitives from the original pilot artifacts and determine whether any occurrence maps, only after freezing, to the A2451/PTC neighborhood. If the exact 16-mer floor is too strict, use a separately versioned follow-up with a predeclared shorter/variable-length rule rather than changing this test retroactively.
support_condition: At least one already-frozen three-domain primitive or an independently preregistered nested primitive maps post-freeze to the A2451-centered PTC neighborhood.
weakening_condition: No exact 16-mer exists there but a separately preregistered shorter/structural primitive transfers across the domains.
falsification_condition: Repeated appropriately powered searches across independent genomes show the A2451/PTC neighborhood is not recoverable as reusable sequence/structural vocabulary under the codebook representation while less constrained regions are.
contamination_boundary: Semantic dependency prediction frozen before inspecting the full original 54 shared-16-mer identities or performing any targeted sequence search around A2451.

validation_stage_1.remaining_preregistered_path: shorter/variable-length follow-up must be separately frozen before execution

validation_stage_2.summary: The exact-14 follow-up reproduced the frozen 5,561 global vocabulary count but found zero target-window hits.
validation_stage_2.remaining_hypothesis_space: Variable-slot/structural-equivalence representations remain untested; no further k lowering is authorized by this result.
